title: Garden and Salt
premise: Emrys Vasquez survives by stealing memories—harvesting them from the sleeping rich and selling them to collectors who crave lives they never lived. When a mute child arrives at their mountain cabin speaking Thornfell's dead first-tongue, Emrys discovers the child's memories are the key to unbinding King Aldric, whose crown is a parasite that devours a soul each generation. Pursued by crown wardens and haunted by the memory-thief who trained them, Emrys must choose between selling the child to buy their own freedom and walking the smuggler roads one last time to reach the salt-cathedral where the binding began. In the end Emrys gives up their own stolen hoard of memories—including every version of who they might have been—to sever the crown, and the child, speaking at last, names them with a word that means both 'thief' and 'keeper'.
about_author: Ivo Eriksen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing confiscated folk manuscripts in a northern border town. Garden and Salt is their second novel, written in the margins of a life spent translating what official histories chose to forget.

chapters.title: The Weight of Borrowed Years
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Emrys completes a routine memory theft from a magistrate, savoring the stranger's childhood garden, then returns to their isolated cabin to find a child asleep on their doorstep, murmuring in a language no living person should know. The beat is unease: Emrys's carefully walled-off life has developed a crack.

chapters.title: A Tongue Older Than Crowns
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Unable to sell a memory they can't read, Emrys takes the child to the scholar Brannoc, who identifies the speech as pre-kingdom Thornfell and goes pale: the child is reciting a binding-litany. Crown wardens arrive asking after a runaway. Beat: dread hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: What the Magistrate Forgot
chapters.summary: POV Emrys, with a flashback in the warden Captain Sera Voss's voice via a stolen memory Emrys replays. Emrys realizes the magistrate they robbed last week was carrying sealed orders about the child. Wardens burn Brannoc's shop. Beat: guilt—Emrys's own greed lit the fuse.

chapters.title: The Smuggler's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Emrys weighs selling the child to Voss against a collector's offer, running the cold math of survival. A quiet scene where the child shares a memory-vision of the salt-cathedral and a king weeping. Beat: Emrys chooses the road, telling themselves it's still a transaction.

chapters.title: Roads That Remember
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The pair travel the Thornfell passes; the child's litany grows stronger near old waystones, and the mountains themselves seem to respond. Voss's wardens ambush them at a river crossing; Emrys escapes by burning a stolen memory of the terrain—losing a piece of their past to save their present. Beat: sacrifice as habit becoming choice.

chapters.title: The Man Who Taught Me to Steal
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. Emrys's old mentor, Corvin, catches up to them—he is the crown's memory-thief and wants the child for the thing in the crown. A duel of harvested memories in a ruined watchtower, each weaponized recollection more intimate than the last. Beat: Emrys confronts the mentor who made them hollow.

chapters.title: Salt in the Wound of the World
chapters.summary: POV Emrys, briefly the child. Wounded, they shelter in the salt-caves beneath the cathedral ruins, where the child finally speaks: her name is Issa, and she is the last unbound vessel of the litany. Emrys confesses what they've stolen from innocents. Beat: the raw honesty before the storm.

chapters.title: The Court of the Hollow King
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. They reach the capital during the king's jubilee and infiltrate the palace through memory-blind servant corridors. Emrys sees King Aldric up close: a man mostly devoured, the crown pulsing like a feeding mouth. Voss corners them—but hesitates, having glimpsed truth in a stolen memory. Beat: the enemy wavers.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: POV Emrys and Issa. In the throne room before the assembled court, Issa begins the litany and the crown fights back, flooding the hall with the devoured kings' screams. Emrys pours their entire hoard of stolen lives into the severing—every borrowed garden, every purchased childhood—burning their archive to nothing. Beat: the climax, all or nothing.

chapters.title: Keeper
chapters.summary: POV Emrys. The crown is ash, Aldric dies human and free, and Voss lets them walk. Emrys, memory-poor and strangely light, leaves the capital with Issa, who names them with the old word meaning both thief and keeper. They plant a garden above the salt-caves. Beat: resolution—identity rebuilt not from what was taken, but what was given.
